fields.meta_title: Volunteer Survey Builder for Nonprofits | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a volunteer survey for your nonprofit: compare satisfaction by role, route new volunteers by availability, and keep every answer.
fields.h1: Build a Volunteer Survey for Your Nonprofit
fields.hero_description: Build a volunteer survey that compares satisfaction across roles and keeps every answer in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Your Volunteer Survey Can Do
fields.features_subheading: Volunteers meet the first two features on a phone after a shift. The other four sit with the coordinator who reads the results.
fields.feature_1:
Questions written for volunteer roles

Describe your program and Emergent writes each question in the type it needs. A dog walker rates the walk schedule on a 1-5 scale, and a new tutor picks open evenings from a list.
fields.feature_2:
One question per screen after a shift

Volunteers open the link on a phone and answer one question per screen. A rating takes a single tap, and the open comment box comes last, for anyone with more to say about the shift.
fields.feature_3:
Scores split by role and site

Tag each response with the volunteer's role and site, and the dashboard averages every question by both. A role that scores well overall but poorly at one site shows up at once.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders to anyone yet to answer

Send each volunteer a personal link and the app tracks who has answered. On the day you pick, it emails a reminder to the rest, and anyone who already answered hears nothing more.
fields.feature_5:
Answers in a database you own

Every response is a row in a database you own, stored next to the volunteer's role, site, and hours. Connect it by API to the volunteer management tool or CRM your team already runs.
fields.feature_6:
The full survey app, on your GitHub

On paid plans, Emergent exports the survey app, its logic, and the dashboard to your GitHub repository. A developer on your team can review the code there or keep building on it.

fields.usecase_heading: What Four Volunteer Surveys Turned Up
fields.tab_content_1:
Front desk volunteers score 2.9 of 5, the lowest role

Harbor Hill Animal Shelter sends its yearly satisfaction survey to 176 active volunteers, and 132 answer. The dashboard splits every score by role. Dog walkers average 4.6, while the 18 front desk volunteers average 2.9 and name late shift schedules in their comments. Coordinator Marisol Brandt reads those answers first.
fields.tab_content_2:
Tomas Reyes is on the Tuesday ESL roster within minutes

Lakeshore Literacy Project asks each new volunteer which evenings they can give and which languages they speak. Tomas Reyes picks Tuesday and Spanish. When he submits, the app adds him to the Tuesday ESL roster and emails program lead Grace Whitfield his answers.
fields.tab_content_3:
The check-in line tops the fix list for 17 of 41 volunteers

After its Saturday river cleanup, Friends of the Clearwater emails a short survey to the 64 volunteers who signed in. It opens on a phone with one question per screen. By Sunday night, 41 have answered. On question 3 of 4, what to fix next time, 17 pick the check-in line and 13 pick gloves and bags.
fields.tab_content_4:
Docent scores reach 4.3 after mentors join in April

The Bramwell History Museum sends its 52 docents the same 5-question survey every quarter. In April, it starts pairing each new docent with a mentor. The average score was 3.6 in Q1 and 3.9 in Q2, and it reaches 4.3 in Q3. Docent manager Owen Pettigrew takes the trend to the board.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Volunteer Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a volunteer survey, build it with Emergent, and act on what your volunteers tell you.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Tell Emergent who answers and why
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide when volunteers hear from you: right after a shift, once a year, or on the day they sign up. Each moment needs its own survey. Keep a post-shift check to 4 questions, and let the yearly satisfaction survey run longer.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Describe the program and the decision the results will feed. Emergent builds the survey from that description, along with its database and a results dashboard. To reword a question later, type the change you want and Emergent updates the survey.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask each volunteer for their role and the site or program they serve, or fill both in from your roster. Those two fields are what let the dashboard show that one role, at one site, is having a hard season.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Use the same 1-5 scale for every scored question, so averages compare across roles and across years. Put a single open comment box last. A volunteer who skips it still leaves a complete set of scores for the dashboard.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send the draft to three volunteers from different roles and watch one of them answer on a phone. Reword any question they read twice, and cut any they ask you to explain. If it takes longer than 5 minutes, trim it.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Send personal links from your roster
fields.howto_step_6_des: Upload your volunteer roster and email each person their own link. The app records who has answered. When you send a reminder after 5 days, it goes only to the volunteers whose answers are still missing.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Within a month of closing, tell volunteers 2 changes their answers led to, such as posting front desk schedules a week earlier. Put the note in the email that thanks them, and give the date of the next survey.

faq_plan.q: What are good survey questions for volunteers?
faq_plan.ref: What are good survey questions for volunteers?

prov.original: What are good survey questions for volunteers?

faq_plan.a: Good ones ask about things you can change: how satisfied volunteers are with their role, whether shift times fit their week, and whether training prepared them for the first day. Ask too whether they would recommend volunteering with you to a friend. Keep the volunteer survey questions under 12 for a yearly survey.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a volunteer survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe the program and the people who will answer to Emergent's AI survey builder, and it builds the volunteer survey with a database and a results page. Before you send it, check that every question maps to a decision your team can make this year.

faq_plan.q: How do I sign up for volunteer surveys?
faq_plan.ref: how do i sign up for volunteer surveys
faq_plan.a: You sign up with the organization that runs the survey, not with the survey itself. Register as a volunteer with the group, and its volunteer surveys reach you at the email address on its roster. For a research study that wants volunteers, sign up through the study's own recruitment page.

faq_plan.q: Are volunteer surveys a limitation in a research paper?
faq_plan.ref: is volunteer surveys a limitation for apa paper
faq_plan.a: Yes, they can be. People who volunteer for a study have different characteristics from the general population of interest, which researchers call volunteer bias. Name it in your limitations section and describe who answered. A church survey that only the most active members fill in carries the same skew.

faq_plan.q: What should a volunteer satisfaction survey measure?
faq_plan.a: It should measure how volunteers feel about the parts of the role you control: the work itself, scheduling, training, recognition, and how staff treat them. Add one question on whether they plan to return next year. Read the comments from everyone who answers no before anything else.

faq_plan.q: Is there a volunteer survey template I can start from?
faq_plan.a: Yes, and on Emergent the template is your own prompt: describe your program and its roles, and Emergent builds a volunteer survey around them. The free tier covers building and publishing it. Copy one of the example prompts on this page and change the program details.

faq_plan.q: What are some volunteer survey examples?
faq_plan.a: Volunteer survey examples beyond the four on this page include a skills inventory, which asks what professional skills people could donate. Another is a check-in for volunteers who have not taken a shift in 90 days. A satisfaction survey for volunteers borrows its shape from an employee satisfaction survey but swaps pay and promotion for shifts and recognition.

faq_plan.q: How often should you run a volunteer survey?
faq_plan.ref: how often do you volunteer survey
faq_plan.a: Run a full volunteer survey once a year, plus a short check after each event or season. Leave at least 3 weeks between any two surveys. Emergent sets no cap on responses, and a 4-question check can go to every volunteer after every shift.

faq_plan.q: How do you get more answers to a volunteer survey?
faq_plan.a: Send it within a day of the shift, keep it short enough to finish on a phone, and send one reminder to the people who have not answered. Say up front how long it takes, such as 3 minutes. For volunteers who already use your Slack workspace, have the survey post that reminder in Slack instead of sending an email.

faq_plan.q: Can a volunteer survey show why people volunteer?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Clary and colleagues proposed 6 functions that volunteering serves and built the Volunteer Functions Inventory to measure them. In their field studies, how well volunteers' experiences matched their motivations predicted satisfaction. An employee engagement survey works on the same idea: ask what people came for, then whether they get it.

plan.angle: The volunteer survey SERP is template galleries and question lists from survey tools and volunteer-management blogs; none shows what a coordinator does with the answers. This page is for the nonprofit volunteer coordinator: it shows four programs using one survey each (satisfaction split by role, an availability intake that routes a new volunteer, a phone survey after a cleanup, a quarterly docent check-in) with real numbers, then gives question advice and the research angle (volunteer bias, why people volunteer) in the FAQ. Every answer is a row in a database the organization owns, with no response cap.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Volunteer Survey for Your Nonprofit'; hero 'Build a volunteer survey that compares satisfaction across roles and keeps every answer in a database you own.' (111 chars, primary, leads with Build); how-to description one sentence: 'Seven steps to plan a volunteer survey, build it with Emergent, and act on what your volunteers tell you.'

intent.evidence: Searchers want questions, templates and examples: FAQ 1 'Good ones ask about things you can change...', FAQ 5 satisfaction measures, FAQ 6 template, FAQ 7 examples, four worked surveys in the tabs, a 7-step how-to.

specificity.evidence: Coordinator vocabulary throughout: 'A dog walker rates the walk schedule on a 1-5 scale', 'Tuesday ESL roster', 'the check-in line', 'posting front desk schedules a week earlier'.

openers.evidence: Full-sentence openers: 'Harbor Hill Animal Shelter sends its yearly satisfaction survey...', 'Decide when volunteers hear from you...', 'Send each volunteer a personal link...'.

craft.evidence: Two ', so' endings (Q5 under limit), no sentence over 40 words; the 'answer to' ambiguity in FAQ 2 is a note.

voice.evidence: Calm and concrete: 'Coordinator Marisol Brandt reads those answers first.', 'anyone who already answered hears nothing more.'

truth.evidence: FAQ 8 'Leave at least 3 weeks between any two surveys' contradicts the same answer's 'a 4-question check can go to every volunteer after every shift', why_description 'the whole roster can answer after every shift, all year', howto_step_1_des 'right after a shift' and FAQ 9 'Send it within a day of the shift'. Claims otherwise inside the menu (alerts, no-caps, database-owned, api-connect, code-export, free-start); volunteer bias and Clary VFI facts match their quoted spans.

distinct.evidence: No sibling primary in a heading; the cleanup tab is a volunteer feedback survey ('Cleanup Events'), not a post event survey page; the intake tab routes to a roster, not a volunteer sign up form.

faq.evidence: 10 questions, each answered first; hub link in item 2; links to church survey, employee satisfaction survey, employee engagement survey; no brand or file format in any question; all 4 secondaries carried; locked items 1-2 verbatim.

findings.quote: Leave at least 3 weeks between any two surveys. Emergent sets no cap on responses, and a 4-question check can go to every volunteer after every shift.
findings.issue: FAQ 8 contradicts itself and the page. Its rule of at least 3 weeks between any two surveys clashes with the next sentence (a check after every shift, so weekly for a weekly volunteer). It also clashes with every other place that times the survey: why_description 'so the whole roster can answer after every shift, all year', howto_step_1_des 'Decide when volunteers hear from you: right after a shift, once a year, or on the day they sign up', faq item 9 'Send it within a day of the shift', and tab_content_3 (a survey after each Saturday cleanup).
findings.fix: Drop the 3-week rule, or limit it to long surveys so the post-shift check is clearly separate, e.g. 'Leave at least 3 weeks between two long surveys; the 4-question check after a shift does not count.' Keep the Emergent sentence.
